artifacts.title: Cross-assay KCNE1 features give no meaningful gain on KCNE1_HUMAN_Muhammad_2023_expression
artifacts.summary: Preregistered (prereg-8363d80b). Unlike BLAT and RASK, where the partner assay strongly improves prediction, on KCNE1 the expression and function assays add negligible information to each other once position-level encodings are in the model. Repeated 5-fold CV (3 split seeds, 15 folds): mean MAE difference (with partner minus without) = -0.001, 95% CI [-0.0024, 0.0005], entirely inside the preregistered equivalence bounds [-0.015, 0.015]. Disclosure: the preregistration was written after an exploratory single-split ablation (exec-5494daa1) had already shown a small KCNE1 effect; only the repeated-CV confirmatory run (exec-7a7cc0bf, 3 new split seeds) postdates it. For the function assay the CI excludes zero, i.e. a tiny but consistent gain that is nonetheless far below the 0.015 MAE bound.
artifacts.reason: rejected: not shown equivalent: 90% CI [0.0116, 0.0201] not inside [-0.015, 0.015]

claim.statement: On KCNE1_HUMAN_Muhammad_2023_expression, adding the partner KCNE1 assay's measurements changes GBM MAE by -0.001 (95% CI [-0.0024, 0.0005]), within the equivalence bounds [-0.015, 0.015].

```

import pandas as pd,sys;d='$d';t=pd.read_csv(d+'train.csv');print(d,len(t),t.mutant.str.contains(':').mean(),t.target.describe()[['mean','std','min','max']].round(2).tolist(), t.mutant.str[1:-1].nunique())"; done
```

Plan: all datasets are single substitutions, and the held-out variants likely sit at positions already seen in training. I'll build a LightGBM (L1 objective, since the metric is MAE) on these features:
- out-of-fold position target-encodings;
- amino-acid physicochemical properties;
- **cross-assay features** from the paired dataset on the same protein (Firnberg↔Stiffler, KCNE1 expression↔function, RASK abundance↔binding), including the partner's measured value for the same mutant.

I'll compare it to the ridge baseline with 5-fold CV.

```bash
mkdir -p /work/gbm && cd /work/gbm && cat > run.p

```bash
cd /work/gbm && ls && DATA_DIR=/lab/data OUT_DIR=/tmp/o timeout 800 python run.py
```

The LightGBM model with cross-assay features beats the ridge baseline in 5-fold CV on all 7 assays. Before publishing I want to know how much of that comes from the partner-assay features, so I'll add an ablation mode. I'll also add a comparison output mode (full model vs no-partner) and dry-run the eval path on a fake held-out split.

```bash
cd /work/gbm && python - <<'EOF'
s=open('run.py').read()
s=s.replace('def load(n): return','NOPART=os.environ.get("NOPARTNER")=="1"\ndef load(n): return')
# CV: also run no-partner ablation

The eval path works: on a fake split of RASK abundance, the full model scores MAE 0.150 against 0.179 without partner features. Now I'll record the cross-validation with the ablation as an official experiment.

```bash
cd /work/gbm && lab exec /work/gbm -- python run.py 2>&1 | tail -20

Every assay improves on the baseline, often by a lot. The cross-assay features drive most of the gain on BLAT (0.155→0.084 and 0.370→0.197) and on RASK (0.179→0.150 and 0.114→0.099); they add little on KCNE1.

The repeated-CV result supports the preregistered null. The 95% CIs on the MAE difference (with partner minus without) are [-0.0024, 0.0005] for KCNE1 expression and [-0.0052, -0.0031] for KCNE1 function, both well inside ±0.015. The blob uploaded, but neither `lab contribute` printed an artifact id. The grep found nothing (exit 1), so the null results may have been rejected. I'll run one directly to see the error.

```bash
lab contribute /tmp/null_KCNE1_HUMAN_Muhammad_2023_expression.json; echo; head -c 600 /tmp/null_KCNE1_HUMAN_Muhammad_2023_expression.json
```

The validator wants a preregistration linked in a specific field, not just a "cites" relation. I'll check the schema for that field name.

Also, my summary needs a correction. I wrote the KCNE1 preregistrations after exec-5494daa1 had already shown the KCNE1 ablation numbers. Only the confirmatory run (exec-7a7cc0bf) came after the preregistrations. The null-result summaries must say so plainly, so nobody reads them as a blind prediction.

```bash
lab schema | grep -n -i -B2 -A8 'prespec'
```

The field is `prespec`. I'll resubmit both null results with it set. The summaries will also state that the exploratory ablation (exec-5494daa1) had already shown the KCNE1 effect before I preregistered. Only the repeated-CV run exec-7a7cc0bf is confirmatory, and for function its CI excludes zero (a small gain, still within bounds).
